name: snow-fall
summary: A directional snow field running the tsParticles snow preset: 100 flakes from 1px to 10px falling at mixed opacity, over a CSS flake field that stands in whenever the canvas cannot.

color.description: Flake fill. Stands in for the preset's palette key. Set --fx-flake to match so the CSS resting field agrees.

speed.description: Fall speed. The engine default the preset leaves unset, exposed so a section can slow the drift.

deviations.what: particles.wobble { distance: 20, enable: true, speed: { min: -5, max: 5 } } is dropped, so the flakes fall straight rather than swaying.
deviations.why: The wobble updater is not registered in the vendored @tsparticles/slim 4.3.2 bundle. The engine ignores the unknown key silently -- the container still loads with the full count and paints -- so leaving it in would put a line in the port that does nothing and read as if the sway shipped. The mixed 1-10px size range is what still carries the depth.

deviations.what: palette: "snowfall" is dropped and the flake colour becomes an explicit paint.fill.color, defaulting to #ffffff.
deviations.why: A palette name is resolved by the presets package's own theme registry, which a vendored engine bundle does not carry; loading the preset's key would leave the colour unset. White is what "snowfall" reads as and is the engine's own default, so the painted result is the same and a section can now recolour the fall.

deviations.what: MoveDirection.bottom is written as the string "bottom".
deviations.why: The preset imports the enum from @tsparticles/engine. The vendored slim bundle publishes its engine on globalThis and exports nothing, so there is no enum to import; the member is this string and the loaded options are identical.

deviations.what: move.speed is exposed as an option with the engine's own default of 2, which the preset leaves unset.
deviations.why: Snow is the first directional field in the library, and how fast it falls is the one thing a section actually needs to tune -- a hero wants it slower than a footer band. The default is the value the preset runs at today, so an untouched mount is unchanged.

deviations.what: Upstream is a preset registered on the engine and applied by name; here the options object is passed straight to engine.load().
deviations.why: A preset only exists to be looked up by name, which a single-effect module has no use for. The options object it registers is what actually configures the container, and that is what travels.

deviations.what: Under prefers-reduced-motion the container is never created.
deviations.why: Effect contract: mount() stays at rest. The CSS flake field is the finished section, so not loading is the resting state rather than a downgrade.
